question: Do repeat customers spend more per order than one-time customers?

semantic.answer:
## No — one-time customers actually spend a bit more per order

Using **average order value** (revenue ÷ orders, revenue includes freight):

| Customer type | Avg. order value (BRL) | Orders |
|---|---|---|
| Repeat customers | 145.63 | 6,118 |
| One-time customers | 161.07 | 92,208 |
| Unmatched/unknown* | 90.38 | 1,115 |

**One-time customers spend ~10% more per order** (R$ 161.07) than repeat customers (R$ 145.63). So repeat buyers don't order bigger baskets — they just come back more often. Since orders are heavily dominated by one-timers (92,208 vs 6,118), this isn't a small-sample fluke.

*A small group of orders (1,115) couldn't be matched to a customer profile — likely edge cases in the data, safe to ignore for this comparison.
semantic.reason: Matches correct figures: 161.07 vs 145.63, correct ranking.

sql.answer:

|---|---|---|---|
| One-time (not repeat) | 92,208 | R$161.07 | R$161.31 |
| Repeat customer | 6,118 | R$145.63 | R$145.88 |

**No — repeat customers actually spend slightly *less* per order** than one-time customers (~R$146 vs. ~R$161, about 10% lower). While repeat customers generate more total revenue over their lifetime (multiple orders), each individual order tends to be a bit smaller in value.
